title: The Miraculousness And Testimony Of The Quran 17th Degree 1st And 2nd Points

questions.question: How are the Qur’an and Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, linked in the first point?
questions.answer: Each shows the truth of the other.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the Qur’an and the life of people in the world?
questions.answer: It changed people deeply and changed how they lived together.

questions.question: Which parts of people does the Qur’an help, according to the passage?
questions.answer: It helps souls, hearts, spirits, minds, and daily life.

questions.question: For how long does the passage say the Qur’an has kept teaching people?
questions.answer: For fourteen centuries.

questions.question: About how many verses does the passage say the Qur’an has?
questions.answer: Six thousand, six hundred and sixty-six.

questions.question: About how many people does the passage say recite it?
questions.answer: More than a hundred million people.

questions.question: What does the passage say the Qur’an does for people’s souls and hearts?
questions.answer: It improves the soul and cleans the heart.

questions.question: What does the passage say the Qur’an does for the mind?
questions.answer: It gives guidance and light.

questions.question: What does the passage say the Qur’an does for life itself?
questions.answer: It brings real life and happiness.

questions.question: Why is the Qur’an called unmatched in the second point?
questions.answer: Because it made a great good change and kept helping people for a very long time.

questions.question: In the third point, what happened to the famous poems hung on the Ka‘bah?
questions.answer: People saw them as much less important than before.

questions.question: What did Labid’s daughter think when she took down her father’s poem?
questions.answer: She thought it was not valuable next to the Qur’an.

questions.question: What is one big idea in the first point about Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him?
questions.answer: His miracles and noble qualities point to the Qur’an being from Allah.

questions.question: What is one big idea in the first point about the Qur’an?
questions.answer: Its truth and wonders show that the Prophet is true.

questions.question: What kind of change does the passage say the Qur’an brought to society?
questions.answer: It brought a bright, happy, and true change.

questions.question: Did the change stay for only a short time or continue for a long time?
questions.answer: It continued for a long time.

questions.question: What does the passage say happens again and again with the Qur’an’s verses?
questions.answer: They are read over and over by many people.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the Qur’an’s effect on people’s inner selves?
questions.answer: It helps them grow better inside.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the Qur’an’s effect on thinking?
questions.answer: It gives direction and understanding.

questions.question: What does the passage call the Qur’an because of these effects?
questions.answer: A great wonder and miracle with no equal.

questions.question: In the third point, what special skill of the Qur’an is being praised?
questions.answer: Its beautiful and powerful way of speaking.

questions.question: What happened to the old famous poems because of the Qur’an’s greatness?
questions.answer: Their high place went down.

questions.question: Where had those famous poems been placed?
questions.answer: On the walls of the Ka‘bah.

questions.question: What can we infer from Labid’s daughter removing the poem?
questions.answer: She believed the Qur’an was far greater than that poem.

questions.question: In the first point, does the passage show one-way proof or two-way proof between the Qur’an and the Prophet, peace be upon him?
questions.answer: It shows two-way proof.

questions.question: What in the Prophet, peace be upon him, supports the truth of the Qur’an?
questions.answer: His miracles, signs of prophethood, and excellent knowledge.

questions.question: What in the Qur’an supports the truth of the Prophet, peace be upon him?
questions.answer: Its miracles and true teachings.

questions.question: Name one area of life the Qur’an changed, according to the second point.
questions.answer: Personal life.

questions.question: Name another area of life the Qur’an changed.
questions.answer: Social life.

questions.question: Name one more area of life the Qur’an changed.
questions.answer: Political life.

questions.question: What does the passage say the Qur’an gives to spirits?
questions.answer: Growth and rising higher.

questions.question: What does the passage say the Qur’an gives to minds?
questions.answer: Light and direction.

questions.question: What does the passage say the Qur’an gives to life?
questions.answer: Life and happiness.

questions.question: Why does the passage present the number of readers and the long time span?
questions.answer: To show the Qur’an’s lasting power and wide reach.

questions.question: What was the result of the Qur’an’s eloquence for the Seven Hanging Poems?
questions.answer: Their honor became much smaller.

questions.question: What feeling did Labid’s daughter show about her father’s poem compared with the Qur’an?
questions.answer: Respect for the Qur’an and less esteem for the poem.

questions.question: According to the first point, what does the Qur’an show about Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him?
questions.answer: It shows he is a true messenger.

questions.question: According to the first point, what does Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, show about the Qur’an?
questions.answer: He shows it is Allah’s word.

questions.question: What kinds of human life were changed by the Qur’an in the second point?
questions.answer: Inner life and outer life.

questions.question: What are some inner parts of a person that the Qur’an helped?
questions.answer: The soul, heart, spirit, and mind.

questions.question: What are some outer parts of life that the Qur’an helped?
questions.answer: Personal life, community life, and public life.

questions.question: What does the passage say many people do with the Qur’an’s verses all the time?
questions.answer: They keep reading them.

questions.question: What can we learn from the Qur’an being read by so many people for so long?
questions.answer: It keeps its importance and helps generation after generation.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the Qur’an compared with other books?
questions.answer: It says no other book is like it.

questions.question: What was special about the old poems mentioned in the third point before the Qur’an came?
questions.answer: They were highly honored and even displayed at the Ka‘bah.

questions.question: What changed after people heard the Qur’an?
questions.answer: Those poems no longer seemed as great.

questions.question: Why did Labid’s daughter take down the poem?
questions.answer: She believed it did not measure up next to the Qur’an.

questions.question: What main idea do the second and third points together teach?
questions.answer: The Qur’an changed lives and also amazed people with its beauty.

questions.question: What kind of revolution does the second point describe?
questions.answer: A deep change in people and society for the better.

questions.question: Did the Qur’an affect only worship or many parts of life?
questions.answer: It affected many parts of life.

questions.question: What does the passage say happens to souls because of the Qur’an?
questions.answer: They are trained and improved.

questions.question: What does the passage say happens to hearts because of the Qur’an?
questions.answer: They are cleaned.

questions.question: What does the passage say happens to minds because of the Qur’an?
questions.answer: They receive light and guidance.

questions.question: What does the passage say happens to life because of the Qur’an?
questions.answer: It becomes full of life and happiness.

questions.question: Why does the passage call the Qur’an a marvel?
questions.answer: Because its influence is great, true, and lasting.

questions.question: In the third point, what does the story about the poems help show?
questions.answer: It helps show the Qur’an’s speech is far superior.

questions.question: Who took down a poem from the Ka‘bah in the passage?
questions.answer: Labid’s daughter.

questions.question: In the first point, what two things prove each other?
questions.answer: The Qur’an and Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him.

questions.question: Which one is said to be a clear proof that the Qur’an is from Allah?
questions.answer: Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him.

questions.question: Which one is said to be a miracle given to the Prophet, peace be upon him?
questions.answer: The Qur’an.

questions.question: In the second point, what did the Qur’an change in people themselves?
questions.answer: Their hearts, souls, spirits, and minds.

questions.question: In the second point, what did the Qur’an change in the way people lived?
questions.answer: Their personal, social, and political lives.

questions.question: What shows that the Qur’an’s influence lasted across many generations?
questions.answer: Its verses have been read by huge numbers of people for fourteen centuries.

questions.question: What is one reason the passage says the Qur’an is unlike any other book?
questions.answer: It keeps teaching, purifying, and guiding so many people.

questions.question: What does the passage say the Qur’an gives to spirits and minds?
questions.answer: Growth for spirits and light for minds.

questions.question: In the third point, what old writings lost honor because of the Qur’an?
questions.answer: The famous poems hung at the Ka‘bah.

questions.question: What does the reaction of Labid’s daughter tell us about the Qur’an?
questions.answer: Its words were seen as much greater than even the best poetry.

questions.question: Which point focuses most on the Qur’an’s effect on human life?
questions.answer: The second point.

questions.question: Which point focuses most on the Qur’an’s beauty in language?
questions.answer: The third point.
